note: Clinician-review evidence catalogue for RunTrack. Running claims are drawn from research/RUNNING-CLINICAL-EVIDENCE.md (R01-R30, verified 2026-10-21); cycling claims from research/CYCLING-TT-FIT-EVIDENCE.md. Grades are pragmatic certainty grades, not GRADE. A clinician must verify applicability before signing.

items.claim: Two-dimensional video is reliable for repeated running-angle measurement but has poor-to-moderate criterion validity against 3-D for most parameters; a smartphone markerless system was invalid for peak hip adduction and knee flexion in runners with patellofemoral pain.
items.source: Leporace et al., J Biomech (R01); Neal et al., Phys Ther Sport (R02)
items.caveat: No study validates the RunTrack camera pipeline. Use same-setup comparisons only; frontal-plane estimates are especially low confidence.

items.claim: Running injury risk is multifactorial and prospective biomechanical evidence is sparse; no single gait variable is a proven cause, and training load is not measured by the app.
items.source: Ceyssens et al., Sports Med (R04); Nielsen et al., Int J Sports Phys Ther (R12)
items.caveat: Risk-factor synthesis; no validated prediction model. History, examination, load and PROMs are required.

items.claim: Increasing step rate by about 5-10% reduces braking impulse, step length, knee energy absorption and modelled patellofemoral force in short-term studies; one RCT in novice runners found prevention of injury, not treatment of existing injury.
items.source: Heiderscheit et al. (R13); Lenhart et al. (R14); Willy et al. (R16); Chan et al., Am J Sports Med (R15)
items.caveat: Acute/short-term biomechanics and one novice-runner prevention RCT. No universal 180 spm target; individual response varies and swing-phase loads can rise.

items.claim: Contact position far ahead of the pelvis is a descriptive braking-posture observation; step-length/cadence manipulation changes braking impulse, but the app's 0.15 threshold is not validated and there is no RCT of overstride correction.
items.source: Heiderscheit et al. (R13); Barton et al., Br J Sports Med (R17)
items.caveat: Descriptive only; do not say overstriding causes injury or that a drill fixes it.

items.claim: Greater peak hip adduction, hip internal rotation, contralateral pelvic drop and reduced hip flexion have been associated with patellofemoral pain in some cohorts; female runners who developed PFP had greater hip adduction prospectively. These are associations, not diagnostic criteria.
items.source: Neal et al., Gait Posture (R05); Noehren et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc (R06); Foch et al. (R07); Mousavi et al. (R09)
items.caveat: Mostly cross-sectional and female-predominant; 2-D frontal-plane validity is poor. Video does not measure hip strength.

items.claim: Knee and ankle kinematics at initial contact and midstance differ between injured and uninjured runners in group studies, but overlap is substantial; markerless kinetics differ from marker-based estimates and the difference grows with speed.
items.source: Neal et al. (R05); Mousavi et al. (R09); Tang et al., J Sport Health Sci (R03)
items.caveat: Group-level association; the app estimates kinematics, not ground reaction force, joint moments or tissue load.

items.claim: Foot and ankle metrics from 2-D markerless tracking are descriptive estimates with the same poor-to-moderate criterion-validity limitations as other 2-D angles; no validated 2-D ankle threshold is established, and the Achilles/plantar kinematic literature is limited.
items.source: Leporace et al., J Biomech (R01); Mousavi et al., Gait Posture (R09)
items.caveat: Do not rank foot/ankle as more or less reliable than other joints from R01/R09; no validated ankle threshold. Report descriptively.

items.claim: Red flags are suspicion triggers for serious pathology, not rule-outs. Cauda equina, fracture, infection, tumour, compartment syndrome and exertional cardiac symptoms require prompt medical assessment rather than gait interpretation or exercise progression.
items.source: Finucane et al., JOSPT (R19); Fraser et al. (R20); Tzortziou et al. (R21); Pelliccia et al., Eur Heart J (R22); Warden et al., JOSPT (R23)
items.caveat: The red-flag framework is grade C overall; the ESC cardiac guideline is grade A for exertional cardiac symptoms. Absence of a red flag does not exclude serious pathology; the clinician determines urgency and work-up.

items.claim: The Lower Extremity Functional Scale has 20 items scored 0-4 (total 0-80, higher is better); the MCID/MDC is about 9 points and typical error about 5.3 points.
items.source: Binkley et al., Phys Ther (R24)
items.caveat: Not running-specific; use the same version and recall period; do not diagnose from a score.

items.claim: The OSTRC Overuse Injury Questionnaire has four items per body area scored 0/8/17/25 (total 0-100, higher is worse) and captures participation, training volume, performance and pain burden.
items.source: Clarsen et al., Br J Sports Med (R25)
items.caveat: Weekly monitoring instrument; no established MCID; not running-specific.

items.claim: The 11-point numeric pain rating scale is a standard pain measure; the MDC and MCID are about 2 points in the validation population.
items.source: Childs et al., Spine (R26)
items.caveat: Not running-specific; recall period matters; do not diagnose from a score.

items.claim: VISA-A and VISA-P are 8-item, 0-100 region-specific tendon questionnaires (higher is better); the original papers establish reliability/validity but not an MCID.
items.source: Robinson et al., Br J Sports Med (R27); Visentini et al., J Sci Med Sport (R30)
items.caveat: Do not invent an MCID; not diagnostic.

items.claim: Return to sport is a continuum with shared risk assessment; specific return-to-run criteria evidence is scarce. The app must not supply a return date or clearance.
items.source: Ardern et al., Br J Sports Med (R28); Silbernagel et al. (R29); Warden et al. (R23)
items.caveat: Consensus/clinical commentary; pain-monitoring evidence is specific to Achilles tendinopathy, not fractures or acute muscle injury.

items.claim: Dynamic 2-D knee angle at bottom dead centre is a practical saddle-height reference; it carries a small systematic bias versus 3-D and several degrees of markerless error.
items.source: Fonda et al., J Sports Sci; Bini & Priego-Quesada, J Sports Sci
items.caveat: Saddle-height method evidence is stronger than injury-outcome evidence; do not diagnose knee pain from an angle.

items.claim: Closed hip angle at top dead centre is a video-fit convention; published video-fit ranges cluster around 55-70 degrees for road and 40-60 degrees for TT/tri, but these are not validated clinical norms.
items.source: MyVeloFit public sample fit report; Velogic Studio triathlon metrics documentation
items.caveat: Commercial convention, not a clinical threshold; rider morphology and event demand vary.

items.claim: Torso angle is a descriptive position measure; published TT/tri ranges vary by source and rider, and a more aggressive angle is not automatically better.
items.source: Velogic Studio triathlon metrics; Pedalyze TT/tri fit guide
items.caveat: Position convention; comfort, power and aerodynamics must be assessed together.

items.claim: Aerobar elbow angle is a fit convention (roughly 85-105 degrees for TT/tri); it is not a validated injury or performance threshold.
items.source: Velogic Studio triathlon metrics; common TT fit practice
items.caveat: Convention only; pad position and shoulder comfort require in-person review.

items.claim: Projected frontal area is not CdA; in field data, silhouette area explained only about half of drag-area variance, and smaller area did not always reduce drag.
items.source: Peterman et al., PeerJ; Maddocks & Walker, Sports Eng
items.caveat: Relative same-camera comparator only; never present a watt figure as a measured saving.

items.claim: Two-dimensional video bike fitting is practical but view-dependent; absolute angles should not be compared across camera setups or to 3-D laboratory values.
items.source: Fonda et al., J Sports Sci; Garcia-Lopez & Abal del Blanco, ISBS
items.caveat: Use same-setup comparisons; markerless error can exceed a 5 mm saddle change.

items.claim: Bike-fit bands are not validated to prevent or treat injury; most advocated adjustments lack experimental injury-outcome evidence.
items.source: Bini & Priego-Quesada, J Sports Sci; Priego-Quesada et al., knee pain in cyclists systematic review
items.caveat: Fit guidance only; pain with swelling, locking, giving way or neurological symptoms needs clinical assessment.
